heading: Replay is one operation
text:
### Replay is one operation [LFST.9.6]

[LFST.9.6] A replayer re-executes an event trace against the engine: it
delivers each inject-class event as a recorded input, re-derives each
compare-class event and byte-compares it against the record ([LFST.9.3.1]),
and treats each structural event as framing ([RFCS.17.5]).

A replay that meets any divergence has failed, and reports
`DS_ERR_FS_DIVERGENCE` ([NERR.13]). Whether the replayer stops at the first
divergence or completes the trace and reports every one it met is the caller's
choice and the implementation's latitude; it does not change the verdict. A
replayer that completes the trace must not report success on the strength of
having finished.

**Rebuilding working memory by re-applying recorded events, without running
the engine, is not a mode of this operation and is not a second one.** A tool
needing the recorded state without the determinism check either replays and
reads the result, or inspects the trace directly ([RFCS.1.2]) — which requires
neither an engine nor the compiled program.
